relevance_note: The paper describes four adult cases of Alexander disease, three with a printed GFAP variant, e.g. 'GFAP gene analysis identified a heterozygous c.250 G>A p.Arg79His missense variant'.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON from values I typed. Labels are the paper's section headings 'Case 1' to 'Case 4'. The paper is a review (footnote: 'This literature review') with four illustrative cases; it gives no patient count as a number, so n_patients_reported is null. Reference 20 cited after each variant is a variant database (Waisman Center), not a prior report of these patients, so cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is null. Case 4 has no GFAP variant or genetic test result reported ('suspected to have possible adult-onset AxD'); he is in scope as a case of AxD in the paper but has no variant row. Case 3's variant is printed as 'homozygous c.740 C>T pSer247Phe' (protein without 'p.'), recorded as printed. Not given rows: the two close relatives of Case 1 with 'reported multiple sclerosis' (no individual detail, not tested, not described as affected by AxD) and the mother of Case 2 (informant only). Case 2's mother's concern that the patient 'might have had an unsteady gait and intellectual disability' is hedged and was not recorded as observed; developmental delay and ataxia are left not reported for Case 2 (the prior diagnosis of spinocerebellar degeneration is not a stated ataxia finding). Ages are decades ('early 40s', 'late 30s'), so ISO fields are null. Case 2 onset is recorded as the presentation in her late 30s although she had febrile convulsions in infancy. Case 1 and Case 4 onset is the age at first presentation. Case 1 'no bulbar features' was used to exclude dysphagia and dysarthria/dysphonia on the checklist; 'no sphincter problems' is narrower than the autonomic composite item, so that item stays not reported; 'full range of eye movements' does not exclude the eye-movement composite (saccades not addressed). 'Periventricular abnormalities' and 'juxtaventricular lesions' were counted as cerebral white matter abnormality but not as periventricular rim. Normal findings recorded as excluded abnormalities (D-27): normal facial expression, full range of eye movements, normal left strength, normal sensation, normal patellar reflexes, preservation of the pons. No contradictions found.
